There was a major error in the prediction models most outlets used: they contained the assumption that different state polls' errors were uncorrelated, so even if a candidate overperformed his polling average in one state, that wouldn't be predictive of overperforming his polling average in another.

The model includes the possibility that errors between states ARE correlated, because there may have been a swing in the voting public that tends in the same direction among demographically similar states. So their model more accurately reflected the chances that the candidate would get a lot of states to break his way, and other polls vastly underestimated that.

This "uncorrelated errors" assumption is also what fucked up the asset valuation models that created the 2008 financial crisis. It's a common problem in statistical modeling.
